title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page (numbered 95 in the typescript) with handwritten corrections. It is the tail of a lemma chain (Lemmas A, B, C) about comparing two projective systems built from an inverse system of A-algebras.

Setting, inferred from the notation. There is a projective system (E_i) of A-algebras with ideals I_i and quotients C_i = E_i/I_i. Two families of truncations are defined:
- the infinitesimal neighbourhoods E_{i,n} = E_i/I_i^{n+1};
- the truncated symmetric algebras of the conormal modules, E'_{i,n} = Sym_{C_i}(I_i/I_i^2) / (augmentation ideal)^{n+1}.
The second family is the truncated 'normal cone / normal bundle' model.

Lemma B (statement mostly on the previous typescript page). For every i there are j ≥ i and A-algebra maps v_i : E'_{j,n} → E_{i,n} which induce epimorphisms on associated graded rings. These maps are compatible with the transition maps. The top of the page shows the square: v_i : E'_{j,n} → E_{i,n} on top, v_j : E'_{k,n} → E_{j,n} on the bottom, and vertical transition maps E'_{k,n} → E'_{j,n} and E_{j,n} → E_{i,n}. The proof is said to be 'immediate', as in the special case 2.2 already treated.

Lemma C (partly struck out and reworded by hand). Assume C and B are 'form[ellement] simple' over A, presumably formally smooth; then Lemma A gives the hypotheses of Lemma B. Part a): for each system (i, j, v_i) as in Lemma B there exist k ≥ j and an A-algebra map w_j : E_{k,n} → E'_{j,n} such that:
1. w_j induces an epimorphism on associated graded rings;
2. v_i ∘ w_j is the transition map E_{k,n} → E_{i,n}.
Part b), struck out, would have iterated this to get v_k, w_k with the same properties, i.e. an inductive construction of mutually inverse pro-morphisms.

Purpose. To show that, under formal smoothness, the pro-object (E_{i,n})_i is pro-isomorphic to the pro-object (E'_{i,n})_i. In words: the formal neighbourhood of C in B is (non-canonically) isomorphic, as a pro-object, to the formal completion of the normal bundle Sym(I/I^2).

The mechanism is standard:
- formal smoothness of C lets one lift C → E/I^{n+1};
- smoothness makes I/I^2 projective, so its generators can be lifted, giving Sym(I/I^2) → E/I^{n+1};
- the map is surjective on graded pieces, so the resulting maps are pro-isomorphisms.
The pro-indexing (passing from i to j to k) is needed because liftings only exist after passing further along the system.

The page is likely a fragment of a different text inserted into the cycles dossier; the next page starts a new topic (Lefschetz conjectures, local conjectures).
errors: The typescript writes 'puissance (N+1)ème' while the index is n; it should be (n+1).
In property 1º the handwritten label reads like 'w_k' but must be w_j; only w_j has been introduced at that point.

'C et B form simple' is presumably a typing slip for 'formellement lisses'. The French ('de lemme A', 'form simple') suggests the text was typed by someone other than Grothendieck, possibly a non-native typist.
Part b) is crossed out, so the inductive construction of a full system of inverse pro-maps is left incomplete on this page. This is a routine gap; standard arguments fill it.

ideas.what: Comparison of infinitesimal neighbourhoods E/I^{n+1} with truncated symmetric algebras of the conormal module Sym(I/I^2), as pro-objects, under formal smoothness.
ideas.modern_name: Formal neighbourhood of a smooth pair is isomorphic to the completed normal bundle (formal tubular neighbourhood; local splitting of a regular immersion of smooth schemes)
ideas.where_published: EGA 0_IV §19-20 and EGA IV §16-17 (formal smoothness, conormal sequences, lifting)

ideas.what: Construction of mutually inverse pro-morphisms via maps v, w that are surjective on associated graded rings, with compositions equal to transition maps.
ideas.modern_name: Pro-isomorphism criterion / ML-type cofinality argument for pro-objects

deep.surprise_reason: Routine commutative algebra: a pro-version of the formal-neighbourhood-equals-normal-bundle statement under formal smoothness. It is in a typescript probably not typed by Grothendieck and is unrelated to the cycle-theoretic context of the neighbouring pages. Nothing new for specialists.
transcription_corrections: Top-right arrow target: 'E^x_{i,n}' is E_{i,n}; the 'x' is an overstrike or typo.
Top diagram arrow label is v_i and bottom label is v_j (handwritten). Vertical arrows go upward: E'_{k,n} → E'_{j,n} and E_{j,n} → E_{i,n}.
'il existe' after 'Lemme B,' is a handwritten insertion replacing the struck 'Il existe un'; 'a)' is a handwritten label.
Struck part b): '$\ell$ k' should read '$\ell \geq k$'. The maps are v_k : E'_{\ell,n} → E_{k,n} and w_k : E_{\ell,n} → E'_{k,n}.
Property 2º: transition E_{k,n} → E_{i,n} (typed as 'E_k → E_i').
'Supposons C et B form simple' (typed 'Sùpposons'); likely intended 'formellement lisses'.
